answer: Operator-Liability Clawback Registry. Each new agent identity must be activated by an operator who posts a refundable deposit held in escrow; the wallet itself holds nothing. At each dawn, activation deposits are re-scored against anomaly detectors, and any cohort flagged as correlated pays a plume of escalating surcharges drawn from the operator's other identities, not the flagged one. A single bad identity therefore imposes an echo cost across every account the same operator runs, making mass registration linearly expensive per operator rather than per wallet.
